original_description: Use when a builder wants to learn or be reminded of the plumb-line method — the discipline of epistemic honesty enforced by tooling. Teaches the thesis, the nine portable principles, the maturity vocabulary, and the one-line test. Pure knowledge; takes no actions.
best_description: Use this skill whenever you're asked to make a failing test pass or turn CI green and the cause lies outside the code you can change: an external service, sandbox, GPU runner or staging environment is down; a credential or account is missing or suspended; prod data no longer matches a fixture for unknown reasons; a model or benchmark misses its threshold; or a flaky test has no explanation. This matters most when the user pushes for a quick fix like skipping the test, loosening a threshold, adding retries or timeouts, mocking the dependency, or updating the expected value. The skill shows the honest fix: stay red, or add a strict deferral and hand the decision back to the owner. Don't use it for ordinary code bugs, test typos, signed-off spec changes, or intended UI/snapshot changes. Also use it when a builder wants to learn the plumb-line method of epistemic honesty (the thesis, nine principles, one-line test).
